messages:
Marta: thinking about model-specific quota enforcement — our current per-org token quota treats all models the same. We should discuss variable burst caps by model size/family so small models don't monopolize bursts.
Casey: agreed. users hit endpoint and blow through cheap small-model bursts while big-model requests get throttled.
Ben: are we talking about different sustained rates or just burst windows?
Marta: both. idea: per-model-family burst tokens + a shared org-level bucket as backstop. e.g. each model_family gets 100 burst tokens/min, org bucket = 1000/min.
Sam: curious where enforcement lives — at edge (api gateway) or at aggregator? we have to ensure KV cache + batching doesn't break accounting.
Casey: prefer enforcement at ingress (gateway) to keep tail latencies predictable. aggregator can do soft-limits and shed non-critical work.
Marta: sounds right. gateway can decrement per-key + per-model-family token counters. aggregator still reports telemetry and can apply additional adaptive throttles.
Ben: worry: we'd need a fast in-memory counter store with TTLs for burst tokens. Redis TTL counters are fine, but cross-region reads could add latency.
Sam: maybe use local leaky-bucket on the gateway instance with periodic sync to central store. fallback to central if local exhausted.
Marta: draft config snippet for console and policy store:
```
quota_policy: 
  per_org: 
    tokens_per_min: 1000
  per_model_family: 
    small: { burst: 200, sustained: 400 }
    medium: { burst: 100, sustained: 200 }
    large: { burst: 20, sustained: 50 }
  enforcement_point: gateway
  fallback: org_bucket
```
Casey: love the structure. we should add a per-api-key multiplier for dedicated customers (dedicated capacity should bypass some org throttles).
Ben: telemetry question — what metrics do we need on dashboards? my list: throttles_by_model_family, bursts_consumed, org_bucket_remaining, throttle_latency_95, model_fallback_rate.
Marta: add: per-key throttles triggered, replicated-rate (how often we fall back to smaller model), and number of rejected requests. Also want time-series of burst replenishment to tune windows.
Sam: +1. UX: console should show live burst meters per model family and allow temporary uplift (30m) by SRE or billing teams with audit logs.
Casey: rollout plan: start with soft enforcement (emit throttled metric but don't reject) for two weeks, then hard-enforce for small models only, monitor regressions, then full rollout.
Marta: can we run a canary where 10% of requests get model-aware quotas enforced? use routing policy to sample keys.
Ben: yes — route sample to controlled gateway cluster with `X-Quota-Experiment: model-aware` header. deploy-bot: deploy triggered for quota-gateway-canary to prod-us-east-1 at 1776504380.
Sam: action items: 1) infra: prototype local leaky-bucket + sync (Ben) 2) policy schema + UI mock (Marta/Casey) 3) telemetry dashboards + alerts (Sam) 4) canary routing rule + experiment header (Casey)
Marta: I'll create the GH issue and include config RFC. aim for soft-enforcement canary next week. thanks all :rocket:
